earlier_scan.source_named: Yang, Cathryn 2017. Introducing Limi: A rising tone is born
earlier_scan.note: Phonological description of Limi (tonal Ngwi/Yi); PDF only in closed hh archive, not located openly.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2017. Introducing Limi: A rising tone is born. In Picus Sizhi Ding & Jamin Pelkey (eds.), Sociohistorical Linguistics in Southeast Asia: New Horizons for Tibeto-Burman Studies in honor of David Bradley, 75-95. Leiden: Brill. DOI 10.1163/9789004350519_006. (Full text recovered from the Wayback snapshot of the author's Academia.edu upload, id 34535383.)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 5.5 'Limi's sound system' (pp. 81-85) gives syllable (C)V+tone, 26 consonants, 8 vowels, and 5.5.3 'Tone': four contrastive tones 24/33/55/21 in modal phonation, all tone combinations in disyllables, allotonic sandhi; the words stress/accent/prominence do not occur anywhere in the chapter.
